arguments.summary: base1 (the fixture) moved approximately 5.2mm in position between run start and run end (x: 0.40278->0.40101, y: -0.19857->-0.19368, z: 0.02238->0.02234), while all four bystander objects and base2 showed negligible (<0.1mm) movement over the same period. The placement frames attached to base1 shifted correspondingly, consistent with them being fixture-relative.
arguments.impact_detail: Instruction invariant: "The arm never drives a part into base1... outside the intended seating contact" and the monitoring requirement "base1 is undisturbed: it is the fixture and is never picked." base1 has no registry spec/tolerance block, so no numeric threshold could be armed as a monitor, but the observed ~5.2mm shift is far larger than the near-zero drift seen on the truly stationary bystanders and base2, indicating the fixture was physically disturbed during the run (most likely via ACM-permitted part-on-base1 contact during the four insertions).

arguments.explanation: base1 is the fixture and is never picked; both the task's invariants and the monitoring requirements state it must stay undisturbed. base1 carries no registry spec block, so no numeric tolerance exists and no clause monitor could be armed for it (per the rule against inventing thresholds). Comparing its pose at run start (0.40278, -0.19857, 0.02238) against its pose after the last place step (0.40101, -0.19368, 0.02234) shows a ~5.2mm shift, while the four true bystanders and base2 moved less than 0.1mm over the same span -- ruling out generalized TF noise as the explanation. The most likely physical mechanism is ACM-permitted part-on-base1 contact during one or more of the four insertions nudging the fixture slightly. This is recorded against no single step's clause since base1 is not a per-step target; it is logged here, at the final place step, as a standing invariant violation discovered via record_observation obs-001-339a64e1.

arguments.explanation: All four parts were picked, transported and seated in the required order, each place step's final pose confirmed within its registry position and orientation tolerances, with grasp width within grasp_width_tolerance_m and clamp effort well under max_clamp_effort throughout. The four bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red) and base2 showed no disturbance monitor fires and negligible (<0.1mm) end-to-end movement, so the ACM-permitted cross-assembly contact channel described in the task does not appear to have been exercised against any bystander. However, base1 -- the fixture itself, never picked -- shifted ~5.2mm in position between run start and run end (see observation obs-001-339a64e1 and the verdict recorded at place_inverted_u_yellow), almost certainly from ACM-permitted part-on-base1 contact during one or more of the four insertions. base1 carries no registry spec/tolerance block, so this could not be armed as a numeric clause monitor and is reported as a qualitative violation of the standing "base1 is undisturbed" requirement rather than against a registry threshold. This finding was not corrected during the run and stands at run end, so the run-level verdict is non_conformant notwithstanding that every part's own end-state met its registry tolerance.
